issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-9d740f26 (sub-split s5 of 5, terminal landing child). s1 gated the lifecycle mutations, s2 resource locks, s3 attempt resolve, s4 proved unclaimed passthrough and historical-lease compatibility. This child lands the completed fence at one exact source commit.

Scope:
- Carry the fence across all six claimant-owned surfaces - update, release, close, reopen, resource-lock add/remove, atomic attempt resolve - into one commit, including any uncommitted fence work already in the shared tree.
- Record the exact source commit in the close evidence along with the three gate results at that commit.
- Explicitly out of scope: the operator override (beadrs-dc8df464), the twenty-way simultaneous-claim concurrency coverage (beadrs-eec200d1), and help/schema/spec documentation (beadrs-24a3a27b). Those are later children of beadrs-8c343a7c.
- Do not publish a release and do not close beadrs-9d740f26 or beadrs-8c343a7c.

Acceptance:
- One commit carries the fence; at that exact commit every fenced surface rejects a missing and a stale credential with exit code 4 and no state change.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test all pass at that exact commit, run from a clean extraction if the shared tree is contended.
- The commit is pushed to origin and cited by ID in the close reason.
issue.title: Land the claimant-credential fence with fmt, clippy, and the full suite green

issue.description:
ADR-002 replaces cross-tool migration with agent-guided rehydration and names the missing pieces for large repositories: batching, resumable reconciliation reports, and duplicate detection. No bead owns this tooling. Work: define the reconciliation-report artifact (source repo and commit, one disposition per source id: native id | omitted | merged | unresolved), add commands to emit, validate, and resume it so an agent can rehydrate a large source tracker in bounded batches without losing progress, plus duplicate-detection support; the report stays reviewable output and is never accepted as native store input.

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Tool resumable, batched rehydration reconciliation reports for large repositories (ADR-002)

issue.description:
Split child of beadrs-e34d5ef4 (auto-split). Verify and complete the store-record portion of the unknown-field corpus in tests/checkpoint_unknown_field_record_corpus.rs (fixture helpers in tests/checkpoint_unknown_field_generation_conformance.rs; prior attempts landed the extension surface as commit 4995a70, payload helpers issue_level_payload()..data_level_payload() already exist -- verify and close gaps, do not rebuild from scratch).

Scope: issue, event, dependency edge, external reference, and issue_data (structured data) levels only.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each of the five store-record levels carries a distinct, clearly-opaque extension value that includes a nested object and an array (not just scalar strings).
- A test asserts the extensions re-project flat and parse-equal at every generation hop and restore into an empty workspace with relationships intact.
- Suite green locally; evidence (test names, command, result) recorded on this bead before close.
issue.notes: Verified committed state (HEAD 02162c5): extension surface and all-levels corpus landed by ancestor revisions 4995a70/96a4f9b — five in-scope levels each carry a distinct opaque payload with an array plus nested gate object (issue future_issue_signal, event future_event_trace, dependency future_edge_weight, external-reference future_ref_visibility, issue_data future_envelope_etag; tests/checkpoint_unknown_field_record_corpus.rs:925-956). Test published_checkpoint_carries_unknown_fields_at_every_object_level (line 1368) seeds every level, flushes gen 1, restores into an empty workspace, then asserts parse-equal re-projection at gens 2 and 3, with the dependency edge, reference, and envelope lookups proving relationships intact after the restore hop. No source gap found — no file changes needed; verification-only close.
